# spp_over_spw_two_clocks: build brief

Space Packets over SpaceWire with two clock domains: the SpaceWire side runs on a 50 MHz port clock, the Space Packet node on the 100 MHz system clock. The Composer inserts asynchronous FIFOs for the packet links.

This brief was generated by the Open Space Composer from the system file `spp_over_spw_two_clocks.composer.json` (catalog `0a7e06a1638b`).
The file holds the system as edited (`instances`, `connections`, `externals`), in `resolved` the netlist it resolves to and in `catalogSubset` the catalog entries of its blocks (interfaces, fields, clocks, generics).
Build a VHDL-2008 top level `spp_over_spw_two_clocks` from `resolved` as described below; everything needed is in the file and in the listed repositories.

## 1. Sources and libraries

Fetch every repository at the given version and compile one VHDL-2008 library per row, in this order:

| Library | Repository | Version | Files | Entities used |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `olo` | https://github.com/open-space-hdl/open-logic-ft | tag `4.7.0-ft.3` (commit `a3c86207790fa91d89e5f02a657f6345de31656e`) | every file listed in `compile_order.txt`, in its order | `olo_base_reset_gen`, `olo_ft_fifo_async` |
| `openwire` | https://github.com/open-space-hdl/openwire | commit `e5142cdb40240f2cbf202529c9f2ccf112038dd6` | the `src/*.vhd` files of every module listed in `component_list.txt`, modules in the listed order | `owr_core` |
| `openrmap` | https://github.com/open-space-hdl/openrmap | commit `4ae4bfe31395ecbc31d5076796fd94bd7cb9de0e` | the `src/*.vhd` files of every module listed in `component_list.txt`, modules in the listed order | `omap_core` |
| `openspp` | https://github.com/open-space-hdl/openspp | commit `da4e97b7ad9e0e8ee1af234d18210cbfdcdac492` | the `src/*.vhd` files of every module listed in `component_list.txt`, modules in the listed order | `spp_core`, `spp_nchar` |

- `olo`: Clone with the submodule 3rdParty/en_cl_fix (git clone --recursive); compile_order.txt lists its files. 4.7.0-ft.3 adds olo_base_chunker and olo_axi_lite_decoder to 4.7.0-ft.2 and changes no other source, so the cores verified with 4.7.0-ft.2 use it unchanged.
- `openwire`: The submodules of the repository (open-logic, uvvm) serve its own tests; a system uses the olo library of the Composer.
- `openrmap`: The submodules of the repository (open-logic, uvvm) serve its own tests; a system uses the olo library of the Composer.
- `openspp`: The submodules of the repository (open-logic, uvvm) serve its own tests; a system uses the olo library of the Composer.
- One `olo` library (Open Logic FT `4.7.0-ft.3`) serves the whole system. The cores were verified with the Open Logic FT tags `4.7.0-ft.2` (openwire), `4.7.0-ft.2` (openrmap), `4.7.0-ft.2` (openspp) (`verifiedWith`); their own `open-logic` submodules are not needed.
- A `modules` file list names one module directory per line, relative to the repository root; blank lines and lines starting with `#` are ignored. The sources of a module are its `src/*.vhd` files. Inside a module the files have no given order: compile its packages (`*_pkg.vhd`) first and let the tool order the rest (GHDL `-i` and `-m`, Vivado and VUnit do), or analyse them in dependency order.
- With GHDL: analyse Open Logic file by file (`ghdl -a --std=08 -frelaxed --work=olo <file>`), import the files of a core library (`ghdl -i --std=08 -frelaxed --work=<library> <files>`) and let `ghdl -m --std=08 -frelaxed <top>` find the order. `-frelaxed` is needed: Open Logic and the cores use constructs that GHDL accepts only relaxed (for example the shared variable of `olo_base_ram_sdp`).
- With other tools follow the order of the table.

- `spw0.Spw` (SpaceWire line, clock domain `link`): Data-strobe line drivers and receivers of a SpaceWire link (LVDS buffers outside the core).

- `spp0.S_Tx[0]` (Space Packet send port, clock domain `sys`): Send port of OpenSPP: one SDU (Octet String Service) or one Space Packet (Packet Service) per stream packet, with the per-SDU side band (APID, packet type, secondary header flag, packet name) in user.
  - `tx0_S_Tx_User_0`: 10:0 APID; 11 Secondary header flag; 12 Packet type (telecommand); 13 Packet name instead of sequence count; 27:14 Packet name.
- `spp0.M_Rx[0]` (Space Packet receive port, clock domain `sys`): Receive port of OpenSPP: one SDU or Space Packet per stream packet, with APID, flags, loss indicator and the user application value in user.
  - `rx0_M_Rx_User_0`: 10:0 APID; 11 Secondary Header Indicator (Octet String Service); 12 Packet Loss or Data Loss Indicator; 13 Double bit error in the receive buffer during this SDU, valid with last; 21:14 User Application value of the CPTP packet (0 without the CPTP layer).
- `spp0.S_AxiLite` (AXI4-Lite register bus, clock domain `sys`): AXI4-Lite register access (32 bit data), for example the register file of a core.

## 3. Architecture

1. Context clause (`resolved.context`): `library ieee;` `use ieee.std_logic_1164.all;` `library olo;` `library openwire;` `library openrmap;` `library openspp;`
2. Declare every signal of `resolved.signals` (one per port of an instance, named `<instance>_<port>_s`, with the type of the port).
3. Instantiate every entry of `resolved.instances` as `<id> : entity <library>.<entity>`: a generic map with the generics whose `default` is false (the value is the VHDL literal in `vhdl`), and a port map with the `actual` of every port. Leave out the ports with `useDefault` (they keep their VHDL `default`). Clocks and resets are port actuals on purpose: never assign a clock to another signal.

## 4. Clocks and resets

| Clock domain | Frequency | Clock | Reset generator |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| System clock (`sys`) | 100 MHz | top-level port `Clk_sys` | `auto_rst_sys` (olo_base_reset_gen, output `auto_rst_sys_RstOut_s`) |
| Port clock (`spw`) | 50 MHz | top-level port `Clk_spw` | `auto_rst_spw` (olo_base_reset_gen, output `auto_rst_spw_RstOut_s`) |
| Link clock (`link`) | 200 MHz | top-level port `Clk_link` | none: no block of the domain has a synchronous reset |

Reset ports (`reset` of the port):

| Port | Reset | Actual | Why |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `spw0.Rst` | asynchronous | `Rst` | Asynchronous reset; the core synchronises its release in every domain. |
| `rmap0.Rst` | synchronous | `auto_rst_spw_RstOut_s` | Synchronous reset in the clock domain Port clock (clock Clk): the output of the reset generator auto_rst_spw. |
| `nchar0.Rst` | synchronous | `auto_rst_spw_RstOut_s` | Synchronous reset in the clock domain Port clock (clock Clk): the output of the reset generator auto_rst_spw. |
| `spp0.Rst` | synchronous | `auto_rst_sys_RstOut_s` | Synchronous reset in the clock domain System clock (clock Clk): the output of the reset generator auto_rst_sys. |
| `auto_cdc_c5.In_Rst` | synchronous | `auto_rst_spw_RstOut_s` | Synchronous reset in the clock domain Port clock (clock In_Clk): the output of the reset generator auto_rst_spw. |
| `auto_cdc_c5.Out_Rst` | synchronous | `auto_rst_sys_RstOut_s` | Synchronous reset in the clock domain System clock (clock Out_Clk): the output of the reset generator auto_rst_sys. |
| `auto_cdc_c6.In_Rst` | synchronous | `auto_rst_sys_RstOut_s` | Synchronous reset in the clock domain System clock (clock In_Clk): the output of the reset generator auto_rst_sys. |
| `auto_cdc_c6.Out_Rst` | synchronous | `auto_rst_spw_RstOut_s` | Synchronous reset in the clock domain Port clock (clock Out_Clk): the output of the reset generator auto_rst_spw. |
| `auto_rst_sys.RstIn` | asynchronous | `Rst` | Asynchronous reset input (polarity from RstInPolarity_g). |
| `auto_rst_spw.RstIn` | asynchronous | `Rst` | Asynchronous reset input (polarity from RstInPolarity_g). |

`Rst` is the asynchronous system reset. A reset generator asserts the reset of its domain at once and releases it synchronously to the clock; a block with an asynchronous reset synchronises the release itself.

## 5. Constraints

Every clock crossing is an Open Logic block. Between the clocks of a crossing a maximum delay applies in both directions, the period of the faster clock, data path only (Open Logic clock crossing principles). Do not declare these clocks as asynchronous clock groups: in Vivado `set_clock_groups -asynchronous` overrides the delay limits.

- False path from `Rst`: Asynchronous reset input; the reset generators synchronise its release.
- False path from `spw0_Spw_DIn`, `spw0_Spw_SIn`: Inputs that spw0 synchronises itself.
- Output registers in the I/O blocks for `spw0_Spw_DOut`, `spw0_Spw_SOut`: Place the output flip-flops of data and strobe in the I/O blocks with matched routing.
- Maximum delay from the clock of `Clk_link` to the clock of `Clk_spw`: 5 ns, data path only (`set_max_delay -datapath_only` in Vivado). Clock crossings of spw0: the period of the faster clock.
- Maximum delay from the clock of `Clk_spw` to the clock of `Clk_link`: 5 ns, data path only (`set_max_delay -datapath_only` in Vivado). Clock crossings of spw0: the period of the faster clock.
- Maximum delay from the clock of `Clk_spw` to the clock of `Clk_sys`: 10 ns, data path only (`set_max_delay -datapath_only` in Vivado). Clock crossings of auto_cdc_c5, auto_cdc_c6: the period of the faster clock.
- Maximum delay from the clock of `Clk_sys` to the clock of `Clk_spw`: 10 ns, data path only (`set_max_delay -datapath_only` in Vivado). Clock crossings of auto_cdc_c5, auto_cdc_c6: the period of the faster clock.
- AMD Vivado: source the script of Open Logic once. It reads the scoped constraints of olo_base_cc_reset, olo_base_cc_bits, olo_base_cc_simple, olo_base_reset_gen and olo_base_ram_sdp wherever the system uses them, also inside the cores. tools/vivado/all_constraints_amd.tcl would also read those of olo_intf_sync, which expect device pins at its input and stop the build (ERROR 18-513) where a block synchronises internal signals with it, as ofb_pa_gty does; a block that synchronises device pins declares its own false path for them. File `src/base/tcl/olo_base_constraints_amd.tcl` of Open Logic.

## 6. Notes from the user guides

**SpaceWire port** (`owr_core`, `spw0`): https://openspacehdl.org/openwire/docs/user_guide.html

- LVDS output buffers for data and strobe and LVDS input buffers with fail-safe biasing belong to the top level; the core contains no I/O buffer.
- Enable the safe implementation of state machines in the synthesis tool.
- Set INT_HOLDOFF and INT_ACK_DELAY for the network before distributed interrupts are used.
- Serve the indication ports before the indication FIFO (16 entries) fills.
- Write registers as 32-bit words; a read that depends on a write waits for the write response.

**RMAP node** (`omap_core`, `rmap0`): https://openspacehdl.org/openrmap/docs/user_guide.html

- Rst is synchronous and high-active; synchronise its release to Clk, for example with olo_base_reset_gen.
- M_RepData, M_Conf and M_User must be served when connected; a stalled output stalls the received packet stream and the link.
- RMAP address bits above AxiAddrWidth_g must be zero in the windows.
- With AxiMaxBeats_g = 1 and AxiDataWidth_g = 32 the memory master issues single transfers only and can drive an AXI4-Lite slave; tie M_Axi_RLast to '1'.

**N-Char adapter** (`spp_nchar`, `nchar0`): https://openspacehdl.org/openspp/docs/user_guide.html

- A received end of packet marker without data characters is discarded.
- A link packet that ends with a beat without valid bytes gets its marker after the bytes of the earlier beats; a link packet without any byte sends nothing.

**Space Packet node** (`spp_core`, `spp0`): https://openspacehdl.org/openspp/docs/user_guide.html

- Rst is synchronous and high-active; synchronise its release to Clk, for example with olo_base_reset_gen.
- After the reset the core initialises both APID tables (2048 clock cycles); packets are sent and delivered once the tables are ready.
- Serve every receive port, or place a buffer behind a port whose user can stall for long.
- TxBufferBytes_g holds the longest SDU of a port, RxBufferBytes_g the longest Space Packet.
- Hold the side band (TUser) of a send port constant during an SDU.
- A last beat without valid bytes (Keep all zero) ends an SDU or packet at the inputs; an SDU without any byte is rejected (0x02). The outputs never carry a beat without valid bytes.
- The user supplies the packet secondary header at the start of the Octet String and keeps the secondary header flag of an APID static.

## 7. Initialisation by software

Register addresses are byte addresses of the AXI4-Lite port of the block; write registers as 32-bit words and wait for the write response before a read that depends on it.

**`spw0`** (SpaceWire port, `owr_core`) through the top-level ports `spw_reg_S_AxiLite_*`:

1. Read ID (0x00): it reads 0x4F575201.
2. Optionally write LINK_SPEED (0x14) bits 7:0 RUN_DIV: the bit period in the Run state in LinkClk cycles (reset value RunDiv_g); choose it for the far end, which samples at most about LinkClk / 1.2.
3. Write PORT_CTRL (0x10) = 0x34 (RECEIVER_EN, DRIVER_EN, LINK_START) to start the link, or 0x38 (AUTO_START) to wait for the far end.
4. Wait for PORT_STATUS (0x18) bits 2:0 LINK_STATE = 5 (Run) before packets are exchanged.

**`rmap0`** (RMAP node, `omap_core`) through the top-level ports `rmap_reg_S_AxiLite_*`:

1. Read ID (0x000): it reads 0x4F4D4101.
2. None needed: with the default generics the target accepts every command to the logical address 0xFE with the key 0x00 on the whole address space (WinInit_g). A flight configuration narrows the logical addresses (TGT_LA 0x010), the key (TGT_KEY) and the windows (WIN_BASE, WIN_LAST, WIN_CTRL), see the register map.

**`spp0`** (Space Packet node, `spp_core`) through the top-level ports `spp_reg_S_AxiLite_*`:

1. Read ID (0x000): it reads 0x53505001.
2. After the reset wait until TABLE_STATUS (0x040) bits 1:0 (TX_BUSY, RX_BUSY) are 0: the core initialises both APID tables (2048 clock cycles).
3. Nothing else is needed: with TxPathDefault_g and RxPathDefault_g every APID has an enabled path to destination 0 and to receive port 0, destination 0 has the Target Logical Address 0xFE (DEST_CTRL 0x400) and the own address is Tla_g. A flight configuration writes the APID tables (TX_TABLE_APID 0x030 and TX_TABLE_ENTRY 0x034, RX_TABLE_APID 0x038 and RX_TABLE_ENTRY 0x03C) and the destinations (DEST_CTRL 0x400 + 0x20 n).

## 8. Checks

No problems found.

## 9. Verification

A smoke testbench `spp_over_spw_two_clocks_tb` (VHDL-2008, no extra libraries):

1. Instantiate `spp_over_spw_two_clocks` and drive `Clk_sys` at 100 MHz, `Clk_spw` at 50 MHz, `Clk_link` at 200 MHz.
2. Hold `Rst` at '1' for 16 cycles of the slowest clock (50 MHz), then '0'.
3. Keep every external input idle: stream inputs with valid at '0', ready inputs of external outputs at '1', bus requests idle, pins at '0'.
4. Run for at least 100 us (the blocks initialise their tables after the reset) and stop the simulation: it must end without failed assertions, and the handshake outputs of the top level (valid, ready) and the line outputs must not be 'U' or 'X' after the reset. Data outputs may stay undefined while their valid is '0'.
5. Where an AXI4-Lite port is external, read the ID register of the block (section 7) and compare it with the documented value.

With GHDL: analyse the libraries of section 1, then `ghdl -i --std=08 -frelaxed spp_over_spw_two_clocks.vhd spp_over_spw_two_clocks_tb.vhd`, `ghdl -m --std=08 -frelaxed spp_over_spw_two_clocks_tb` and `ghdl -r --std=08 -frelaxed spp_over_spw_two_clocks_tb --stop-time=100us --assert-level=error --ieee-asserts=disable` (`--ieee-asserts=disable` silences the warnings of the numeric package about metavalues before the reset).

Optional end-to-end test, after the initialisation of section 7:

- SpaceWire port (`owr_core`): Loop the SpaceWire line back (Spw_DOut to Spw_DIn, Spw_SOut to Spw_SIn) or connect a second port, start the link and wait for PORT_STATUS LINK_STATE = 5 (Run).
- Space Packet node (`spp_core`): Send one SDU on a send port (APID 0x123, for example) and expect it on receive port 0 with the same APID in user bits 10:0, once the APID tables are ready.

blocks.name: Space Packet node
blocks.summary: Space Packet Protocol (CCSDS 133.0-B-2) with the CPTP layer of ECSS-E-ST-50-53C: send and receive ports with Octet String or Packet Service, APID routing and a register file.
notes: Rst is synchronous and high-active; synchronise its release to Clk, for example with olo_base_reset_gen.
After the reset the core initialises both APID tables (2048 clock cycles); packets are sent and delivered once the tables are ready.
Serve every receive port, or place a buffer behind a port whose user can stall for long.
TxBufferBytes_g holds the longest SDU of a port, RxBufferBytes_g the longest Space Packet.
Hold the side band (TUser) of a send port constant during an SDU.
A last beat without valid bytes (Keep all zero) ends an SDU or packet at the inputs; an SDU without any byte is rejected (0x02). The outputs never carry a beat without valid bytes.
The user supplies the packet secondary header at the start of the Octet String and keeps the secondary header flag of an APID static.

init.text: After the reset wait until TABLE_STATUS (0x040) bits 1:0 (TX_BUSY, RX_BUSY) are 0: the core initialises both APID tables (2048 clock cycles).

Nothing else is needed: with TxPathDefault_g and RxPathDefault_g every APID has an enabled path to destination 0 and to receive port 0, destination 0 has the Target Logical Address 0xFE (DEST_CTRL 0x400) and the own address is Tla_g. A flight configuration writes the APID tables (TX_TABLE_APID 0x030 and TX_TABLE_ENTRY 0x034, RX_TABLE_APID 0x038 and RX_TABLE_ENTRY 0x03C) and the destinations (DEST_CTRL 0x400 + 0x20 n).

Enable the managed data paths: for every APID write TX_TABLE_APID (0x030), read TX_TABLE_ENTRY (0x034), write it with ENABLE and DEST, read it again; the same with RX_TABLE_APID (0x038) and RX_TABLE_ENTRY (0x03C) with ENABLE and PORT; write the destinations (DEST_CTRL 0x400 + 0x20 n).

blocks.endToEnd: Send one SDU on a send port (APID 0x123, for example) and expect it on receive port 0 with the same APID in user bits 10:0, once the APID tables are ready.

generics.label: Stream width
generics.description: Width of all streams; follows the connected packet link unless set by hand.

generics.label: Send ports
generics.description: Number of send ports.

generics.name: NumRx_g
generics.label: Receive ports
generics.description: Number of receive ports.

generics.label: Send port services
generics.description: Bit p for send port p: '1' Octet String Service, '0' Packet Service.

generics.name: RxOctetString_g
generics.label: Receive port services
generics.description: Bit p for receive port p: '1' Octet String Service, '0' Packet Service.

generics.name: TxBufferBytes_g
generics.label: Send buffer
generics.description: Buffer of each send port; holds the longest SDU of the port. DataWidth_g / 8 times a power of two.

generics.name: TxMaxPackets_g
generics.label: Send buffer SDUs
generics.description: SDUs a send buffer holds.

generics.name: RxBufferBytes_g
generics.label: Receive buffer
generics.description: Receive buffer shared by all receive ports; holds the longest Space Packet. DataWidth_g / 8 times a power of two.

generics.name: RxMaxPackets_g
generics.label: Receive buffer packets
generics.description: Packets the receive buffer holds.

generics.name: Encapsulation_g
generics.label: CPTP layer
generics.description: CPTP layer of ECSS-E-ST-50-53C; false removes it.

generics.name: NumDest_g
generics.label: Destinations
generics.description: Destinations of the CPTP layer.

generics.name: SpwAddrBytes_g
generics.label: SpaceWire address bytes
generics.description: Maximum target SpaceWire address of a destination in bytes.

generics.name: MaxLength_g
generics.label: Maximum packet length
generics.description: Reset value of the maximum packet length.

generics.name: RoundRobin_g
generics.label: Round robin
generics.description: Reset value of the multiplexing scheme: '0' fixed priority (port 0 first), '1' round robin.

generics.name: Tla_g
generics.label: Target logical address
generics.description: Reset value of the own target logical address of the receive filter.

generics.name: TxPathDefault_g
generics.label: Send paths enabled
generics.description: Every APID has an enabled path to destination 0 after reset. A flight configuration enables the paths by software.

generics.name: RxPathDefault_g
generics.label: Receive paths enabled
generics.description: Every APID has an enabled path to receive port 0 after reset. A flight configuration enables the paths by software.

generics.name: ClkFreqHz_g
generics.label: Clock frequency
generics.description: Clock frequency for the scrubbers of the APID tables.

clocks.label: Clock
clocks.description: All of the core; one beat per cycle on every path.

sideband.description: Parameters of the SDU, held constant during the SDU.

blocks.name: Asynchronous FIFO (SECDED)
blocks.summary: FIFO between two clock domains whose memory is protected by a SECDED code; optionally triplicated synchronisers.

constraints.note: AMD Vivado: source the script once; it reads the scoped constraints of the Open Logic base entities (clock crossings, reset generator, RAM).
